paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus restores. Peter had said he wouldn't leave Jesus, and then he did. Now Jesus asks him three times, "do you love Me?" and each time hands him a job: "Feed My lambs," "Shepherd My sheep," "Feed My sheep." (John 21:15-17) I think Jesus isn't keeping score here. I think He's saying, "I still have work for you."

Then Peter asks about somebody else, "Lord, what about him?" and Jesus answers, "what is that to you? You follow Me!" (John 21:21-22) Baker, that one is for all of us, because I have ruined whole batches staring at the next counter over. Your road is yours, and Jesus walks it with you. Follow Him on that road and leave the comparing at the door.

The rumor about the other disciple is a good warning too. People heard what they wanted, but Jesus did not say that he would not die (John 21:23). So we stay careful and hold onto what He actually said. And the writer says there are so many more things Jesus did that not even the world itself would have space for the books (John 21:25). Friend, that is why you keep coming back to the Word, and why the story isn't over, because the Supper is still being prepared.
